solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A change of face tint giving unnatural appearance

indicators.note: a change of these words means their letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone altering their complexion with makeup ends up looking artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' acts on OF FACE TINT, giving FFECTATION after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-on manner or look, assumed rather than natural, is a pose of this kind.

clue.text: Reportedly in favour of disc power for this type of vehicle

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the next word is heard rather than written, so its sound gives the number

parts.note: in favour of means for
a wheel is a disc
drive means motive power

explanation.surface: Someone backs disc-driven power for some vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR (in favour of) said aloud is FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles whose engine turns all their wheels, such as off-roaders, are of this type.

clue.text: Timeless concise language

indicators.note: timeless says the letter standing for time (T) is taken away

parts.note: concise means terse

explanation.surface: A description of a pithy language that never dates.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish Gaelic, or Scottish Gaelic, is known by this old name.

clue.text: Threatening plants first scrambled round tops of fences in dark

indicators.note: round says the mixed letters go around the other piece
scrambled says the letters of first are mixed up
tops of takes the leading letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Menacing plants clamber over fence tops after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threatening plants' are Wyndham's walking killer plants; 'scrambled' acts on the word first, and 'round' wraps it about the three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wyndham's novel features walking, stinging plants that menace humanity.

clue.text: Heartless canny character in Oz?

parts.note: the Wizard of Oz figure made of metal (canny as in made like a can) who lacks a heart

explanation.surface: A cold, shrewd person in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Canny looks like shrewd and Oz like Australia, but it means made like a can, in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal woodman of Baum's story longs for the heart he was built without.

clue.text: Sultanate featured in romance

indicators.note: featured in says the letters appear within the word romance

explanation.surface: A sultan's realm appears in a love story.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf state on the Arabian peninsula is ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Means to pass over water in nine pots arranged in stages, holding gallons

indicators.note: in says the whole assembly is placed inside the word for stages

parts.note: stages means steps

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged letters contain the abbreviation
arranged says the letters of nine pots are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Water stored in nine pots set out in tiers, containing several gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' looks like the pots' contents, but belongs to the definition; the first 'in' is a link, the second puts everything inside stages.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of stones placed in a stream lets walkers cross without wading.

clue.text: Expert's calling for stimulation

parts.note: a pro is an expert
a calling is a vocation

explanation.surface: A professional's chosen career offers stimulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goads or incites a reaction is a stimulus to act.

clue.text: Mission number one, to retract post about 'reactionary' Humphrys, perhaps

parts.note: a mission is a quest

indicators.note: to retract means to draw back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mast is a post

indicators.note: reactionary, moving backwards, says the letters are reversed

parts.note: RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A political tale of a mission retracting a post about the reactionary broadcaster Humphrys.
explanation.walkthrough: John Humphrys was a long-time host of the BBC quiz Mastermind.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz host is a person who poses questions to contestants; Humphrys is an example.

clue.text: Before celebration Amin changed new parliament's last ruling

parts.note: pre means before
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: changed says the letters of Amin are rearranged
last takes the final letter of the word parliament

explanation.surface: Idi Amin changes a parliament's final ruling before a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Amin 'changed' gives MINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling force is the dominant or prevailing one.

clue.text: Oars in line at start of sculling

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: at start of takes the opening letter of sculling

explanation.surface: Oars lined up at the start of a sculling race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oars' looks like a plural noun, but it is a verb: oars as in propels a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To oar a boat is to propel it with oars, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: POW camp housed in regal fortress overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown says the hidden letters are read backwards
housed in says the letters sit inside the words regal fortress

explanation.surface: A prisoner-of-war camp held in a fortress after a regime was overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'housed' in the definition, but 'housed in' signals the hidden letters, so the definition is just 'POW camp'.
explanation.definitionFit: German camps for captured officers in the world wars were known by this name.

clue.text: Wide boy's odds on kind of drip

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A wheeler-dealer is betting odds-on a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a flashy petty crook or black-market trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is the old British slang term for a flashy small-time dealer.

clue.text: Work out clue, maybe, with distribution of spare letters

indicators.note: distribution of means the letters of spare are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Solving a crossword clue by shuffling the spare letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse a sentence's grammar or a clue's parts is to break it down.

clue.text: Fellow's clever story

parts.note: able means clever

explanation.surface: A clever man's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tale, often with animals and a moral, like Aesop's.

clue.text: Papers, in review: 'Has red transformed ultra-conservatives?'

indicators.note: in review, looked back over, says the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of has red are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper reviews ask whether the reds have become right-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in review' turns ID into DI; HAS RED 'transformed' gives EHARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who resist all change to the last ditch are hardline traditionalists.

clue.text: Old woman's murderer turned psychotic

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old woman

indicators.note: turned says the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Cain was the first murderer in Genesis

explanation.surface: A mother's killer has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes CAIN into NIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildly deranged person is a madman; here used as an adjective, crazed.

clue.text: Get on successfully in vale

definitions.meaning: Latin for goodbye, used as a parting word

explanation.surface: Prospering in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vale' looks like a valley, but it is Latin for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on well is to do so; the Latin parting word means goodbye.

clue.text: Nearly all of Scottish promontory is hard and unyielding

indicators.note: nearly all of says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Mull of Kintyre is a Scottish headland
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A rocky Scottish headland is tough and unbending.
explanation.walkthrough: A mull is a Scottish promontory, as in the Mull of Kintyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn like a mule, refusing to give way.

clue.text: The solution is imminent when one sees this!

definitions.text: The solution is imminent when one sees this!

parts.words: The solution is imminent when one sees this!
parts.note: to see light at last, as the idiom says, means the end of a problem is near

explanation.surface: A solver feels close to cracking it.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to see daylight' means to begin to see a way out or an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing natural light at the end of a tunnel is the idiom for nearing an answer.

clue.text: Components of arms found in river island, not British

indicators.note: not says the letter for British is left out

parts.note: the Humber is an English river estuary

explanation.surface: Weapons discovered on an island in a river, but not British ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-arm bones, plural of humerus, are parts of the arms.

clue.text: Inherently insane Roman fiddler

indicators.note: Inherently says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mad Roman emperor who played the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the emperor fiddled while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is said to have played music while Rome burned, earning this label.

clue.text: Spud's underground root tip

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway

indicators.note: tip takes the first letter of root

explanation.surface: A potato's subterranean root end.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a swollen underground stem, the classic example of this plant part.

clue.text: Two-faced German?

indicators.note: two-faced says the name looks the same from either end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A deceitful German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-faced' looks like deceitful, but means the name reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A common German man's first name, as in Bismarck.

clue.text: Feeling a back strain?

indicators.note: back says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: an air is a feeling or impression, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a backache is a strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AIR A into ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a melody, and an operatic solo song is one.

clue.text: Book list shows published journal

parts.note: a log is a list or record

explanation.surface: A list of books appears in a published journal.
explanation.definitionFit: An online diary or column posted on the web is a published journal.

clue.text: Twice Verne recreated light imaginary place

indicators.note: recreated says the doubled letters are rearranged
twice means the name Verne is taken two times

parts.note: to light is to land, settle

explanation.surface: Jules Verne's tales twice recreated in a light fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: VERNEVERNE 'recreated' gives NEVERNEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's fantasy island, also any idealised fantasy realm.

clue.text: In conversion a light is mostly good for one depicting saints

indicators.note: in conversion means the letters are changed into a new order
mostly says the last letter of good is dropped

explanation.surface: A religious conversion lit up for a painter of saints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' good gives GOO; A LIGHT IS plus GOO 'In conversion' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of saints' lives is one who studies and portrays holy figures.
